_comment: Cross-client category canonicalisation (T-108, T-274). ONE file, read by BOTH test suites:
web/src/lib/categories.test.ts imports it, Android's CategoryCanonTest reads it from the repo
root the way ExpenseMathTest reads expense-arithmetic.json.
canonicalisation: among the casings seen for one case-insensitive category key, the
most-frequent one wins; a tie breaks by UTF-16 code unit (Kotlin's default String order,
NEVER a locale-aware compare) — the smaller string wins. A category_order entry's casing is
authoritative over both and always overrides the vote for its key.
the same way name order does (shared-test-cases/name-order.json) — by UTF-16 code unit, not a
locale collation. This is a plain code-unit sort of the canonical names, NOT the accent/case
folding name-order.json pins; the two are deliberately different rules for different screens.
The web client used to break both of these with String.localeCompare, which agrees with the
code-unit order whenever counts differ or names share a first letter's case, and disagrees
exactly on a genuine tie or a mixed-case comparison ('Obst' vs. 'obst', 'Äpfel' vs. 'Bananen') —
which is exactly why it went unnoticed until now.

canonical_names.name: a two-way tie breaks by code unit: uppercase sorts before lowercase
frequency still wins over the tie-break
a category_order entry overrides the vote even when it would lose a tie
an outright majority needs no tie-break

autocomplete_order.name: an uppercase-accented name sorts by its raw code unit, not after plain ASCII (T-274)
a tied casing's winner (uppercase, by code unit) still sorts case-sensitively
three distinct categories, plain ASCII order
